title: Unannounced Trump Organization deals: Hungary, Serbia and others in the filings
summary: Forbes's July 2025 reading of corporate filings did point to unannounced Serbia and Hungary deals, and CREW's August 2026 FOI requests name DT Marks Budapest LLC and DT Marks Budapest Member Corp. But no partner, fee or project has been disclosed for either country, the Serbian entity's name was not found, and the 2025 disclosure (as summarised by PolitiFact and CNBC) shows no Hungary or Serbia income. The richest new link is Eagle Hills (Mohamed Alabbar), the Gulf partner on both Kushner's Trump-branded Belgrade project and Orbán's dropped EUR 12.3B Grand Budapest plan. Hungary won a run of US sanctions decisions in 2025, but no source ties them to the family's business. Serbia's US relief came only after the Belgrade project collapsed.

sub_claims.statement: Forbes: corporate filings point to unannounced Trump deals in Serbia and Hungary
sub_claims.finding: Single-source (Forbes, 24 Jul 2025, read via snippets and licensed editions): 'Corporate filings point to at least three other unannounced deals—in Abu Dhabi, Serbia and Hungary.' Forbes also says entities were registered after the election for Pune, Noida, Gurgaon, Hungary's capital and the Philippines.

sub_claims.statement: DT Marks Budapest LLC and DT Marks Budapest Member Corp. exist
sub_claims.finding: Documented: CREW's Aug 2026 FOI requests to Hungary's Trade Licensing Office and Ministry of Construction and Transport name both companies and ask for records on a Trump property in Budapest and on Kushner's role in 'Grand Budapest'. Exact formation date not found; Forbes places it between the Nov 2024 election and Jul 2025. Audit: the entity names are documented only through CREW's own FOI request letters (and Forbes's reference to a Budapest entity); no corporate-registry record or second outlet naming 'DT Marks Budapest' was found, so formation date, state and officers remain unverified.

sub_claims.statement: Partner and fee for the Hungary entity
sub_claims.finding: No partner, project or fee is disclosed. The 2025 disclosure's licensing countries (PolitiFact; CNBC via Times Brasil) are Oman, Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Romania, the Philippines, Vietnam and India: no Hungary. The OGE form itself was not read.

sub_claims.statement: Eagle Hills (Alabbar) links the Belgrade and Budapest projects; Kushner floated for Grand Budapest
sub_claims.finding: Documented for each leg. Eagle Hills and Affinity announced the Trump-branded Belgrade project ~17 Jan 2025. Orbán met Vučić in Belgrade on 18 Jan 2025; VSquare's source (single-source) says he briefed Vučić on Grand Budapest. Hungary announced the EUR 12.3B Grand Budapest contract with Eagle Hills on 20 Jan 2025. A VSquare government-linked source said Kushner 'may become involved' (Trump-Tower-style skyscraper); another said Affinity was 'not currently involved'. Kushner's role is unverified. Orbán met Alabbar in Abu Dhabi.

sub_claims.statement: Grand Budapest dropped before any Trump deal surfaced
sub_claims.finding: Documented: Budapest's municipal company exercised a pre-emption right over Rákosrendező and the government abandoned the project in early 2025. Linking the DT Marks Budapest entities to this project is inferred: no source says so, though CREW asks about both.

sub_claims.statement: Don Jr. visited Vučić and Budapest in spring 2025 to expand family business ties
sub_claims.finding: Documented: Don Jr. met Vučić in Belgrade on 11 Mar 2025 and dined with him again in late April. On 25 Apr 2025 he had what Telex describes as a brief, informal encounter with FM Szijjártó in Budapest (officially nothing was discussed; closed to the press) and spoke at the 'Trump Business Vision 2025' forum (organised by Zoltán Aczél/Portfolio; expected meeting with 4iG chairman Gellért Jászai). Bloomberg framed the trip as expanding family business ties. No deal was announced. His spokesperson rejected conflict suggestions.

sub_claims.statement: US decisions favourable to Orbán's Hungary in the same period
sub_claims.finding: Each decision documented; link to the family's business inferred (timing only). Rogán delisted 15 Apr 2025, ten days before Don Jr.'s visit. Paks II sanctions relief ~29 Jun 2025 (Hungarian account). One-year Russian oil and gas sanctions exemption 7 Nov 2025 (Orbán claimed open-ended). 'Financial shield'/swap claimed 9 Nov 2025 and denied by Trump in Dec 2025. Vance campaigned for Orbán, who lost on 12 Apr 2026 to Magyar. Post-election status of the US exemption not found. Audit: the Rogán delisting date (posted 15 Apr 2025 US time, reported 16 Apr in Europe) is confirmed by Bloomberg, Telex and RFE/RL. State gave no reason beyond 'inconsistent with U.S. foreign policy interests'. Senators Shaheen and Warren said the Global Magnitsky Act requires 15 days' prior notice to Congress before a termination. No source links the delisting to Don Jr.'s trip; the pairing remains our timing observation (inferred).

sub_claims.statement: Serbia: Trump licence for the Belgrade project, entity and fee
sub_claims.finding: Documented that Kushner said he and Eric Trump 'agreed on licensing' (Jan 2025) and that Eric said the contract would be with the developer, not the state. Vreme refers to a contract signed at the outset and asks whether Kushner could claim ~EUR 50M (no claim confirmed). The licensing entity's name, formation date and fee were not found, and no Serbia income appears in the 2025 disclosure summaries.

sub_claims.statement: Serbia: US policy (NIS sanctions, tariffs) relative to the Belgrade project
sub_claims.finding: Decisions documented; the pairing is inferred and cuts against a favour. The NIS deferral was refused in Oct 2025 while the project was alive. The project collapsed 15 Dec 2025. MOL-Gazprom Neft heads of agreement for 56.15% signed 19 Jan 2026. OFAC repeatedly extended licences; on ~5 Nov 2026 it gave MOL a licence to 28 Feb 2027 for preparatory work only, not closing. The US suspended its 35% tariff on Serbia in Jul 2026 and launched a strategic dialogue on 17 Jul 2026.

sub_claims.statement: NIS resolution routes through Hungary's MOL with possible ADNOC minority
sub_claims.finding: Documented that MOL is the buyer and that ADNOC may take a minority stake. The cross-link to the Trump-family story (a Hungary-Serbia-UAE loop alongside Eagle Hills) is our inference; no source asserts it.

sub_claims.statement: Complete list of DT Marks/DTTM entities formed since Nov 2024 with country, partner and fee
sub_claims.finding: Not reconstructible from public reporting available here. Documented: DT Marks Abu Dhabi (30 Jan 2025, Damac, $5M) and DT Marks Al Raha Beach (Jul 2025 per CREW, Damac, $5M). Single-source: DT Marks Doha (Forbes Türkiye), DT Marks Tbilisi ('inactive', CREW), and the India and Philippines entities (Forbes). DT Marks Vietnam took $5M (C59). CREW counts at least 34 second-term companies, eight tied to UAE, Vietnam and India developments. CNBC: four new licensing LLCs earned $20.25M in 2025. Neither names Hungary or Serbia.

corrections: The brief calls Hungary and Serbia 'deals'; the filings show entities, not signed deals with known partners or fees.
The 'financial shield'/currency swap was claimed by Orbán and denied by Trump in Dec 2025; it is not an established US decision.
The Russian-energy exemption was for one year per the White House, not open-ended as Orbán claimed.
The NIS relief came after the Belgrade project collapsed and is tied to a sale to MOL; the waiver was refused in Oct 2025 while the project was alive.
denials_and_context: White House: the president's dealings are unrelated to the Trump Organization; no conflicts of interest.
Trump Organization: it only licenses its brand to private developers; its 2025 ethics policy bars only deals directly with foreign governments.
Eric Trump: the Belgrade hotel contract would be with the developer, not the Serbian state.
Don Jr.'s spokesperson rejected conflict-of-interest suggestions over his Serbia visit.
Affinity and Eagle Hills did not answer VSquare; a source said Affinity was not involved in Grand Budapest.

Orbán was the administration's closest EU ally, which gives an ideological explanation for the Hungary decisions. The Rogán designation was a last-days Biden action, and Hungary and Slovakia also hold EU pipeline-oil carve-outs.
forbes.com, citizensforethics.org, congress.gov, govinfo.gov and the Delaware register could not be fetched here; findings rest on search snippets from several outlets.
